concept: Floodlit scrapyard portrait under smoke loop
creativeDirection: Night location photography in a real scrapyard, using one cast portrait group as the anchor and folding the other sleeves into fixtures, paint, and sky details within a single plausible editorial shot.
scene: An after-dark industrial scrapyard yard with muddy ground, stacked wrecked cars, scattered scrap, and rough embankments, seen at eye level as a cleanly lit editorial photograph. Four men stand close in the near-middle ground, leaning slightly inward toward the camera as on their sleeve, with a bright looping smoke trail high in the cloudy night sky above them. Around the yard are a few sharp, recognisable details from other sleeves: a painted open-mouth graphic on the side of a dented metal container, a small heraldic shield sign fixed to a fence panel, and a glossy purple biomorphic object resting on a scrap heap.

elements.element: the four men leaning inward toward the camera, kept recognisable as the group portrait
the scrapyard-like muddy wrecked street as the main location, with abandoned vehicles, litter, puddled earth, and rough embankments
a bright looping smoke trail arcing across the cloudy sky above the yard
a large painted open mouth graphic on the side of a battered metal skip or container
a small geometric heraldic shield sign bolted to a wire fence
a smooth glossy purple biomorphic form lying among the scrap
soft monochrome tonal restraint in the portrait lighting
subtle yellow-to-red heat in parts of the yard lighting

prompt: After-dark scrapyard yard, eye-level medium-wide view, camera close enough to read faces clearly, muddy ground and rough embankments with stacked wrecked cars and scattered scrap, no other people anywhere. The primary subject is the four men from reference image 1, standing in the near-middle ground and leaning inward toward the camera as in their sleeve, long hair, dark jackets, recognisable faces properly lit, their pose and gaze preserved while placed in this yard. Build the location mainly from reference image 3: a ruined muddy industrial backstreet turned into a real scrapyard with abandoned vehicles, litter, puddled earth, dented metal, and rough sloping sides. Add a bright looping smoke trail from reference image 6 high across the cloudy sky above them; a large painted open-mouth graphic from reference image 5 on the side of a battered metal skip; a small geometric heraldic shield from reference image 7 as a sign bolted to a fence panel; and a smooth glossy purple biomorphic object from reference image 8 lying among the scrap at natural size. Photographic realism, night location photography, crisp editorial detail, physically plausible materials and scale, no collage feel. Compose as an eye-level medium-wide group portrait with the men occupying the lower middle of frame and the yard wrapping around them, layered depth but not a corridor, clean separation of subject and background. Light with floodlights and sodium yard lamps, balanced so every cast face is clear and natural, with the smoke loop and support details still readable. Palette of mud brown, rust, dark green, sepia, sodium yellow, red accents, purple-violet, and clouded blue-grey; mood tense, strange, gritty, and cinematic. Reference map for people (the album images are attached in this numbered order): reference image 1 shows four young men leaning over the camera in dark jackets. Copy each of these faces directly from that numbered reference image - same face, bone structure, hair, expression, and styling - rather than drawing a new person from the description. Nobody from reference images 2, 3, 4 appears in the picture: use those images only for colour, setting, and objects, and add no figures, faces, or silhouettes from them. Hard constraints (override any conflicting source material): Create a single cohesive 16:9 image, not a grid, contact sheet, row of covers, or collage of separate panels. Do not reproduce the album sleeves as framed thumbnails, posters, record covers, or pictures on a screen, monitor, or television. A sleeve's abstract graphics, shapes, patterns, and colours may be painted onto the walls, doors, floor, or objects of the place as part of its decoration, without any lettering. Show no sleeve's faces, heads, or figures as a picture, mural, display, sign, relief, or silhouette anywhere; transform the sleeves' non-text visual motifs into one original composition. Include no readable text or lettering of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, code, glyphs, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, labels, or signage. Feature only adults and avoid gore, wounds, body horror, medical or anatomical imagery, blank or milky eyes, nudity, sexual content, weapons, and hate symbols; reinterpret any sensitive source motif abstractly. When a source includes a person, closely match their visible appearance and likeness to the reference image, preserving recognisable facial features, hair, skin tone, clothing, and styling, and their apparent age: every person is shown as the adult they are on the sleeve, never younger, smoothed, or more boyish or girlish. Keep each reference person in the pose, expression, and gaze the sleeve shows, and keep every identifiable face sharp, lit, unobscured, and in focus: no motion blur, long-exposure smearing, steam, fog, shadow, crowding, or shallow depth of field over a reference person's face. Expose the image cleanly whatever the light: every person's face well lit and readable, shadows that hold detail, and clear colour, with no murky underexposure, crushed blacks, heavy film grain, digital noise, or dust-and-scratches texture. Add no incidental plants: no flowers, potted plants, planters, climbing vines, ivy, hanging foliage, hedges, lawns, flower beds, or greenery framing the edges or carpeting the floor, unless the description above explicitly asks for that plant as part of a source motif or the year treatment. Dress the scene with the materials of the place itself - stone, metal, concrete, wood, fabric, glass, water, equipment - rather than vegetation. Everyone in the picture is photographed in the same place, at the same moment, under the same light as the rest of the scene, in full colour and with the same lens and grain: do not carry over a sleeve's own backdrop, studio lighting, backlit flare, monochrome, colour cast, or print texture onto the person. Each person stands inside the scene at the scale of the space around them, never as an oversized cropped head or bust looming at the edge of the frame over a distant scene, and never washed in red, blue, or other coloured light. Depict each identifiable reference person only once in the entire composition; do not repeat or clone them as another figure, reflection, mirror portrait, poster, billboard, screen, photograph, painting, silhouette, or background face. The only exception is repetition visibly intrinsic to one source cover: keep that repetition within that single source motif and do not echo the person elsewhere. The only people anywhere in the image are the reference people named in the reference map, and of those only the ones whose faces are clearly visible in their reference. Add no one else: no extra band members, musicians, staff, bystanders, passers-by, crowd, audience, background or out-of-focus figures, and no hands, arms, legs, or shadows of unseen people. Never complete a person who is hidden, cropped, turned away, blurred, or only partly visible in a reference with an invented face or body - leave that person out entirely. Photograph the reference people from roughly eye level, at three-quarter length or closer, in the near or middle ground, so each of their faces is large, sharp, and clearly recognisable in the final frame: never from directly above, and never as small distant figures.
